mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with tighter financial conditions, which suppresses equity risk premiums and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month, and SPX outperforms the risk-free rate by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) coincides with elevated wage growth expectations, which raises the cost of capital and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% over the prior 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when PAYEMS increases by <5%, or wage growth surprises are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in HOUST (industrial production) by at least 2% in the prior quarter indicates weakening aggregate demand, which is associated with negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when HOUST growth ≥2% in the quarter prior.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in INDPRO (industrial production) for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which reduces market optimism and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO recovers in the following month without a similar multi-month decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% suggests labor market strength and tighter monetary policy expectations, which produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when UNRATE > 4.5% in prior month and remains above 4.0 for 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in GDPC1 (GDP) above 2% indicate accelerating demand, which boosts equity valuations and yields positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% each month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically significant when GDPC1 growth is ≤2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in RSAFS (retail sales) above 5% in the prior month signals consumer confidence recovery, which supports equity valuations and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when RSAFS increases by <3% in prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) by 0.5% over three months indicates deflationary pressure, which reduces real earnings and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when CPIAUCSL increases by >0.2% over the same period.
